gmat-focus-readiness-check-016.prompt: Harbor City started weekly curbside compost pickup last March. By December, methane readings at the municipal landfill had fallen 18 percent. Officials conclude that the compost program caused the drop and should be expanded citywide. Which assumption is required by the argument?

options.a: No other landfill change, such as new gas flares, began in the same window and actually cut methane.
options.b: Households in every neighborhood will sort food scraps as carefully as the pilot zone did once the service is rolled from the pilot zone to the remaining wards.
options.c: Compost collection costs less per ton than expanding remaining landfill capacity over the next capital-planning cycle the public works board will vote on.
options.d: Methane readings at dumps in neighboring cities rose over the same nine months while Harbor City's own dump was the only site adding weekly organics pickup.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-016.explanation: The officials treat the methane drop as an effect of compost pickup. That causal leap fails unless competing landfill changes in the same period can be ruled out.

distractorExplanations.b: Citywide sorting diligence would matter for expansion success, not for the causal claim already made.
distractorExplanations.c: Relative cost is a budget issue, not a required premise of the methane-cause argument.
distractorExplanations.d: Other cities' methane trends are unused in the officials' reasoning about Harbor City.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-017.prompt: After Riverton Hospital opened quiet nap rooms for night nurses, medication-dispensing errors on night shifts fell 22 percent. Administrators conclude that nap rooms improve night-shift safety. Which finding, if true, most strengthens the argument?

options.a: Day-shift nurses asked for similar rooms even though their error rate was already low and asked facilities to copy the night-shift floor plan.
options.b: Nurses who used the rooms logged fewer microsleep lapses on wearable monitors than nurses who skipped them.
options.c: The hospital's cafeteria extended hours during the same months the rooms opened offering hot meals that night staff had requested for years.
options.d: Night-shift hiring bonuses rose, attracting more newly licensed nurses to Riverton, so the night roster mixed more novices with veteran dispensers.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-017.explanation: A physiological pathway—fewer microsleeps among actual room users—ties the rooms to alertness, which is the proposed cause of fewer errors.

distractorExplanations.a: Day-shift demand does not show that night errors fell because of naps.
distractorExplanations.c: Cafeteria hours are an independent change that could confound, not confirm, the causal story.
distractorExplanations.d: New hires could explain fewer errors without any effect from nap rooms.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-018.prompt: A consulting firm reports that analysts who keep a handwritten daily planner finish more client memos than analysts who rely only on digital calendars. The firm therefore plans to require paper planners for every analyst. Which finding, if true, most weakens the plan's reasoning?

options.a: Paper planners cost more per year than the firm's current calendar licenses when purchased in bulk through the office-supply vendor.
options.b: Some analysts dislike the look of the proposed planner's cover design and asked whether a monogram could be added at checkout.
options.c: High-output analysts already prefer paper tools; the planner use is a marker of drive, not its cause.
options.d: Digital calendars sync more reliably with clients' time zones than paper books do, which matters for scheduling calls but not for memo counts.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-018.explanation: If planner use merely tags already-productive people, forcing planners on others will not raise memo output. That selection confound undercuts the causal recommendation.

distractorExplanations.a: Cost objects to the rollout, not to the claim that planners cause higher output.
distractorExplanations.b: Cover taste is an implementation gripe, not a challenge to the causal inference.
distractorExplanations.d: Sync convenience may favor digital tools but does not explain the memo-count gap.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-019.prompt: Every marshal at the Riverfest parade wears an orange sash. Keiko is wearing an orange sash today. Which conclusion follows from these two statements alone?

options.a: Everyone wearing an orange sash today is a Riverfest marshal, including visitors who borrowed a sash for photographs.
options.b: Keiko is serving as a marshal at the Riverfest parade because she happens to be wearing the marshals' color today.
options.c: Keiko is definitely not a marshal at the Riverfest parade merely because many non-marshals also own orange sashes.
options.d: Keiko's marshal status cannot be settled from the two statements alone.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-019.explanation: Membership implies the sash, not the reverse. A sash wearer may or may not be a marshal, so nothing about Keiko's role is entailed.

distractorExplanations.a: This illicitly converts the original conditional from marshals to all sash wearers.
distractorExplanations.b: This affirms the consequent: a sash does not prove marshal status.
distractorExplanations.c: Nothing in the premises rules Keiko out of the marshal group.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-020.prompt: Every prize-winning pastry chef I have interviewed never completed a culinary degree. Therefore, skipping culinary school raises a baker's chance of winning major prizes. Which option most accurately describes a flaw in the reasoning?

options.a: It samples only winners who skipped school and ignores winners with degrees and non-winners who also skipped.
options.b: It never defines pastry as distinct from bread baking in professional kitchens when describing who counts as a contestant in those contests.
options.c: It assumes prize juries always prefer rustic techniques to classical ones when they score plated desserts at invitation-only shows.
options.d: It treats culinary degrees as more expensive than private apprenticeships when comparing culinary school with hotel apprenticeships.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-020.explanation: The speaker generalizes from a biased slice of winners and never compares base rates among degree-holders or unsuccessful dropouts, so the causal claim is unsupported.

distractorExplanations.b: A pastry/bread definition gap is unused in the argument's leap to causation.
distractorExplanations.c: Jury taste is not the stated basis of the conclusion.
distractorExplanations.d: Tuition cost is irrelevant to whether skipping school raises prize odds.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-021.prompt: Critics insist that a higher statutory wage floor must shrink manufacturing payrolls. Yet in three counties that raised the floor last year, covered-plant headcount held steady. Which finding, if true, most undermines the critics' generalization?

options.a: The three counties already had stronger unions than the national manufacturing average, which might make those plants unlike typical nonunion shops.
options.b: Managers met the higher wage by trimming perks, not jobs, and output per worker rose.
options.c: Nearby counties that kept the old floor also reported fewer open vacancies, which does not show that the wage floor left headcount intact.
options.d: Plant managers in the three counties praised the new floor in local newspapers, which is cheap talk rather than a payroll measurement.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-021.explanation: If firms absorbed the wage through perks and productivity rather than layoffs, a higher floor need not shrink payrolls, which directly undercuts the critics' necessity claim.

distractorExplanations.a: Prior union strength could make the counties unrepresentative, which would help critics, not undercut them.
distractorExplanations.c: Parallel vacancy drops elsewhere do not show that higher wages leave headcount intact.
distractorExplanations.d: Public praise is cheap talk and does not measure actual employment effects.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-022.prompt: A seed firm says its new inoculant lifts soybean yield 30 percent, citing one last-season trial on a single farm. To evaluate that claim, it would be most useful to know which of the following?

options.a: The retail price the firm intends to charge per treated acre if dealers bundle it with the firm's other seed treatments.
options.b: The family name of the grower who hosted the demonstration plot or whether that grower had hosted prior promotional plots.
options.c: Whether matched control acres used the standard inoculant under the same weather and soil.
options.d: How many agronomists the seed firm employs in its marketing division relative to rival seed companies in the same sales region.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-022.explanation: A yield jump is credible only if comparable untreated or standard-treated acres isolate the inoculant from weather and soil. A control comparison is the decisive missing fact.

distractorExplanations.a: Price speaks to adoption, not to whether the 30 percent figure is causal.
distractorExplanations.b: The grower's name does not test the trial's experimental design.
distractorExplanations.d: Marketing headcount is irrelevant to the scientific reliability of the yield claim.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-023.prompt: Unit sales of vinyl records have risen for three years while streaming subscriptions have also grown. Which finding, if true, best resolves the apparent tension?

options.a: Average streaming audio quality has improved with new codecs, which would pull more listening toward phones and speakers.
options.b: Entry-level turntables have become cheaper in electronics stores, which might lift vinyl hardware without explaining streaming.
options.c: Used-record shops have closed in several midsize cities, which would pressure vinyl demand rather than lift both series.
options.d: Many subscribers buy vinyl as display objects and gifts, not as substitutes for daily streaming.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-023.explanation: If vinyl is bought for collecting and gifting while streaming covers daily listening, the two goods are complements for many buyers, so both series can rise together.

distractorExplanations.a: Better streaming quality would, if anything, pull listening away from physical discs.
distractorExplanations.b: Cheaper turntables might lift vinyl alone; they do not explain simultaneous streaming growth.
distractorExplanations.c: Shop closures would pressure vinyl sales downward, deepening rather than resolving the tension.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-024.prompt: A treasury argues that cutting the statutory rate on small-firm profits will raise total tax receipts, because owners will stop hiding cash sales. Which assumption does the argument require?

options.a: Newly reported income will more than offset the mechanical loss from applying a lower rate.
options.b: Every small firm currently conceals the entirety of its cash receipts, rather than concealing only a fraction of their cash sales.
options.c: Large corporations will not demand a matching rate cut in the next budget cycle if small-firm owners successfully lobby for the new rate.
options.d: Owners will hire extra bookkeepers once the statutory rate falls to handle the extra invoices that newly reported sales create.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-024.explanation: Receipts rise only if the extra reported base outweighs the lower rate. Without that magnitude assumption, the treasury's conclusion does not follow.

distractorExplanations.b: The argument needs some previously hidden income, not total concealment by every firm.
distractorExplanations.c: Later political demands from large firms are outside the stated revenue mechanism.
distractorExplanations.d: Bookkeeper hiring is not required for the underreporting-to-reporting story.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-025.prompt: Deep-sea ecologists mapping cobalt-rich crusts found that nodule fields host long-lived sponges whose filtration keeps near-bottom water unusually clear. In a trial strip where a collector robot removed nodules, sponge cover collapsed within months and sediment plumes drifted onto adjacent unmined plots. Filter-feeding fish then left those plots even though nodules there were untouched. Larval sponges settled slowly, and models put recovery of filtration function on the order of decades. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Cobalt crusts regenerate as quickly as coastal oyster reefs after a winter storm once collector robots finish a first pass across the crusts.
options.b: Nodule mining can harm filter feeders on plots the robot never scraped.
options.c: Fish abandon nearby plots only because engine noise scares them for good after the trial robot has left the mapped nodule field.
options.d: Larval sponges settle faster on scraped sediment than on intact nodule pavement once the collector has stripped the trial strip of nodules.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-025.explanation: Plumes reaching unmined plots, followed by fish leaving those plots, show damage beyond the scraped strip. Slow larval return supports lasting functional loss rather than quick recovery.

distractorExplanations.a: Decadal recovery models contradict a storm-fast crust rebound like oyster reefs.
distractorExplanations.c: The text ties fish exit to sediment and sponge loss, not to a permanent noise scare.
distractorExplanations.d: Slow settlement after scraping contradicts a preference for scraped sediment.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-026.prompt: Platform courier apps classify riders as independent contractors and historically left crash insurance to the riders. After several cities required platforms to carry occupational accident cover, some apps introduced per-delivery safety fees. Riders in those cities reported fewer unpaid medical bills after crashes, but weekly take-home pay fell for riders who already bought private cover. Platforms argued the fees merely passed through a legal cost; rider groups said the fees exceeded the premium increase. Which inference is most strongly supported?

options.a: Mandatory accident cover raised every rider's weekly take-home pay, including riders who already carried private crash policies.
options.b: Private insurers stopped selling policies to couriers once cities acted after the city rules required occupational accident cover.
options.c: A safety fee can leave some already-insured riders financially worse off.
options.d: Platforms invented the fees only to punish riders who unionized after a few cities required platforms to carry crash cover.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-026.explanation: The passage states unpaid medical bills fell while take-home pay fell for riders who already had private cover, so the fee can harm that subgroup even if crash bills drop.

distractorExplanations.a: The already-insured group's pay drop contradicts a universal take-home gain.
distractorExplanations.b: Nothing says private insurers exited the courier market.
distractorExplanations.d: Union punishment is not mentioned; the platforms cite a legal pass-through.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-027.prompt: Desert harvester ants lay pheromone trails to seeds, but they stop reinforcing a trail when returning ants meet a jam at the nest entrance. In lab arenas, colonies facing a clogged nest switched faster to a farther seed pile than colonies with a clear entrance, even though the near pile still held food. When researchers artificially widened the entrance, the near pile was depleted first. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.a: Harvester ants abandon pheromones whenever any nestmate is injured and then ignore seed piles that still have remaining food.
options.b: The farther pile always contains more calories per seed than the near pile, which is why clogged colonies switch to the farther pile.
options.c: Entrance widening was effective only because it changed the seeds' smell, rather than by changing how ants respond to nest jams.
options.d: Nest-entrance congestion can redirect foraging even when a near pile remains.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-027.explanation: The clogged-entrance switch to a farther pile, reversed when the entrance is widened, shows congestion itself reroutes foraging while food remains nearby.

distractorExplanations.a: Injury is never cited as the cue that stops trail reinforcement.
distractorExplanations.b: Calorie differences between piles are not reported.
distractorExplanations.c: The design changes entrance width, not seed odor, as the experimental lever.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-028.prompt: When people are given a windfall labeled 'bonus,' they spend more of it on luxuries than when the same sum is labeled 'rebate,' even though both labels describe cash already in hand. In one experiment, rebate-labeled funds were more often parked in savings accounts, while bonus-labeled funds bought restaurant meals. The pattern persisted after researchers equalized the timing of receipt. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Mental labels on identical cash can change how readily people spend it.
options.b: Restaurant meals always yield more utility than savings account interest, so the bonus label cannot be what moved restaurant spending.
options.c: People spend rebates more freely than bonuses when timing is held constant, which contradicts the finding that rebate funds were saved.
options.d: Windfalls raise luxury spending only if they arrive on a weekend, rather than when the cash is labeled bonus versus rebate.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-028.explanation: Equal cash with different labels produced different spending versus saving, with timing matched, so the labels themselves shift consumption. The rebate group saved more, not less.

distractorExplanations.b: The passage reports spending patterns, not a utility ranking of meals versus interest.
distractorExplanations.c: Rebate-labeled funds were parked in savings, the opposite of spending more freely.
distractorExplanations.d: Weekend timing is not discussed; receipt timing was experimentally equalized.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-029.prompt: City-center roofs painted white reflected more sunlight than dark asphalt roofs, cutting afternoon indoor temperatures in uncooled rooms. A later trial added shallow trays of sedum on some white roofs; those plots ran cooler still, but only on dry days. After heavy rain, the planted trays stayed wet into the next afternoon and then released stored heat, erasing the extra cooling. Street-level air temperatures barely moved in either trial. Which inference is most reasonable?

options.a: White paint fails to cool any indoor room in a dense downtown after dark asphalt is replaced on the same downtown blocks.
options.b: Planted trays add cooling mainly in dry weather and can reverse after rain.
options.c: Street-level air always falls as soon as rooftops are painted white once white paint is applied to the same uncooled rooms.
options.d: Sedum trays work only because they make roofs darker than asphalt, which would undermine the reflectance point of the white paint.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-029.explanation: The extra cooling from plants appears on dry days and disappears after rain when stored heat is released. Indoor gains from white paint still occurred; street air did not fall.

distractorExplanations.a: Uncooled rooms did run cooler after white paint, so indoor cooling is not a total failure.
distractorExplanations.c: Street-level air barely moved, so a reliable street-air drop is unsupported.
distractorExplanations.d: White plus plants is not a darkening relative to asphalt; reflectance is the point of the paint.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-030.prompt: In a pain trial, volunteers who believed they had received a strong analgesic showed reduced activity in spinal pain pathways even when the injection was saline. Telling a second group that the injection was inert produced no spinal change, although both groups had identical needles and waiting times. When the first group's belief was later reversed, spinal signals returned toward baseline. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.a: Saline injections treat nerve injury more reliably than opioid drugs in volunteers who never reported a change in believed dose.
options.b: Needles and waiting times, not beliefs, produced the spinal change, since both groups had identical needles and waiting times.
options.c: Expectancy can alter measurable spinal pain signals, not just self-report.
options.d: Reversing a belief never restores spinal activity toward its baseline after researchers told the first group the injection was inert.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-030.explanation: Belief of analgesia changed spinal signals; an inert-label group with the same needle did not; reversing belief moved signals back. That pattern isolates expectancy from the injection itself.

distractorExplanations.a: The study does not compare saline with opioids as treatments for nerve injury.
distractorExplanations.b: Matched needles without the belief produced no spinal change, so hardware is not the cause.
distractorExplanations.d: The reversal condition moved signals toward baseline, contradicting 'never restores'.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-016.prompt: Historians of inland transport note that nineteenth-century canal companies often lobbied against early railways, claiming trains would devastate farm prices by flooding markets. In districts where rails arrived first, however, dairy output rose because milk could reach cities before spoiling. Canal tonnage in those districts later recovered by shifting to coal and grain, goods that tolerate slower hauls. Passenger coaches on canals collapsed and did not return. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Railways reduced every canal cargo to zero within a single season of opening, including coal and grain that later returned to the waterway.
options.b: Dairy farmers opposed railways more fiercely than canal shareholders did in the districts where rails arrived before the canals did.
options.c: Coal and grain spoiled as quickly as milk on warm canal barges, which is why dairy, not coal, had to move onto the trains.
options.d: Rails could complement canals by taking time-sensitive goods while slow bulk stayed on water.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-016.explanation: Dairy growth plus later canal recovery in coal and grain, alongside lost passenger traffic, shows a split: speed-sensitive goods moved to rail while bulk stayed. Total canal collapse is denied by the recovery.

distractorExplanations.a: Later recovery in coal and grain contradicts a total, immediate zeroing of canal cargo.
distractorExplanations.b: The passage never ranks dairy farmers' lobbying against shareholders'.
distractorExplanations.c: Coal and grain are cited as tolerant of slow hauls, the opposite of milk-like spoilage.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-017.prompt: Excavators at a highland pass recovered drilled marine-shell beads in layers dated centuries before local agriculture. The nearest shore lies several weeks' walk away, and the beads' drill-hole wear matches pieces found in a coastal cemetery of the same period. Animal-bone collagen from the highland hearths shows no marine diet. A few unfinished bead blanks appear only at the coast, not at the pass. Which inference is best supported?

options.a: Finished ornaments moved inland through exchange rather than from a coastal diet at the pass.
options.b: Highland foragers harvested shellfish themselves during seasonal sea camps, even though hearth collagen shows no marine protein signal.
options.c: Bead blanks were manufactured at the pass and later carried to the coast, even though unfinished blanks appear only at the shore.
options.d: The coastal cemetery postdates the highland layers by many centuries, even though wear on the drill holes matches the same period.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-017.explanation: Wear-matched coastal beads inland, no marine diet, and blanks only at the coast together indicate finished goods traveling uphill, not local shellfishing or highland manufacture.

distractorExplanations.b: Absent marine collagen argues against highlanders eating shellfish from sea camps.
distractorExplanations.c: Blanks only at the coast contradict manufacture at the pass.
distractorExplanations.d: The text dates beads and cemetery to the same period, not a later cemetery.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-018.prompt: Employees who join a firm's optional lunchtime yoga series report fewer migraine days than employees who never join. The wellness director concludes that yoga reduces migraines and wants to make the series mandatory. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: The yoga instructor is popular in the firm's internal social club, which might explain attendance without explaining migraines.
options.b: Joiners already had fewer migraines and better sleep before the series began.
options.c: The studio space could hold only half the workforce at once, so making the series mandatory would still need extra rooms.
options.d: Nearby firms offer discounted gym memberships rather than yoga, which does not explain this firm's joiner versus nonjoiner gap.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-018.explanation: If joiners were already healthier, the migraine gap is selection, not a treatment effect, so mandating yoga would not be justified by these numbers.

distractorExplanations.a: Instructor popularity might explain attendance, not the migraine comparison's causal meaning.
distractorExplanations.c: Room capacity is a logistics limit, not a confounder of who reports fewer migraines.
distractorExplanations.d: Other firms' gym perks do not explain this firm's joiner-versus-nonjoiner gap.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-019.prompt: A nutrition newsletter claims that drinking two cups of matcha daily raises scores on a working-memory task, citing volunteers who already consumed matcha and outscored abstainers. Which finding, if true, most weakens the causal claim?

options.a: Matcha costs more per serving than supermarket black tea, which might limit who drinks it without explaining memory scores.
options.b: Some volunteers disliked the grassy taste of ceremonial-grade powder, which would reduce consumption rather than inflate memory scores.
options.c: Matcha drinkers also slept longer and practiced meditation, both independently linked to memory scores.
options.d: The memory task used shapes rather than words as the items to recall, which both drinkers and abstainers completed in the same session.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-019.explanation: Sleep and meditation are alternate causes that can produce the score gap without matcha being responsible, which undercuts the newsletter's causal leap.

distractorExplanations.a: Price does not explain why drinkers outscored abstainers on the task.
distractorExplanations.b: Taste dislike would, if anything, reduce consumption, not create a spurious memory benefit.
distractorExplanations.d: The stimulus type does not itself introduce a confound between drinkers and abstainers.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-020.prompt: Clearwater's council says a new waterfront arena will revive nearby shop rents because visiting fans will linger on the promenade. Which assumption is required?

options.a: The arena's construction will finish before the next municipal election, which is a political deadline, not the rent-revival mechanism.
options.b: Nearby shop owners already sell team merchandise in their current stores, which is unused in the claim that fans will linger outside.
options.c: Hotel occupancy downtown has been falling for three consecutive summers, which is a separate lodging trend, not promenade spending.
options.d: A substantial share of fans will spend time and money on the promenade, not only inside the arena.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-020.explanation: Rent revival via promenade lingering requires that fans actually exit onto the promenade and spend. If they stay inside, the council's mechanism fails.

distractorExplanations.a: The election calendar is politically relevant but not required for the rent mechanism.
distractorExplanations.b: Existing merchandise sales are not needed for the fan-lingering story.
distractorExplanations.c: Hotel occupancy is a separate downtown indicator, not a premise of promenade spending.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-021.prompt: A school board wants to drop an end-of-year writing exam because scores correlate weakly with later college grades. Which finding, if true, most strengthens the board's plan?

options.a: The exam mainly rewards handwriting speed, a skill college seminars rarely grade.
options.b: Parents in the district generally prefer multiple-choice tests to essays when the board discusses whether to keep the writing exam.
options.c: Nearby districts still administer a similar writing exam each spring, which does not show that this exam is a poor college signal.
options.d: Printers in the school library often jam during exam week, which is an administration hassle rather than a validity critique.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-021.explanation: If the exam measures a skill colleges do not use, weak correlation is expected and dropping it is more justified than if it measured valued writing.

distractorExplanations.b: Parental format preference is not evidence that the exam fails as a college signal.
distractorExplanations.c: Neighboring practice does not show this exam is a poor measure.
distractorExplanations.d: Printer jams are an administration hassle, not a validity critique.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-022.prompt: Conservationists long treated habitat fencing as the default for a rare grassland bird. A new field program moved eggs to predator-free islands; fledging rates there exceeded fenced mainland nests, but returning adults later failed to find mates because island choruses were too small. Geneticists warn that a few island lineages could dominate. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Fencing mainland nests always produces more fledglings than any island move, even though island fledging exceeded the fenced mainland nests.
options.b: Raising fledging success can still leave a population demographically fragile.
options.c: Island choruses grew large enough to guarantee mates for every returning adult, even though returning adults later failed to find mates.
options.d: Geneticists now recommend replacing all mainland habitat with island colonies, even though the warning is about a few island lineages dominating.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-022.explanation: Higher fledging with later mate shortage and lineage-dominance risk shows that a nest-success gain can still leave a fragile population. Mainland fencing is not shown to be universally worse.

distractorExplanations.a: Island fledging exceeded fenced mainland nests, so fencing is not always superior.
distractorExplanations.c: Adults failed to find mates because choruses were too small, contradicting a guarantee.
distractorExplanations.d: The genetic warning is about lineage dominance, not a call to abandon all mainland habitat.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-023.prompt: Office workers who bring a standing mat report less afternoon back tightness than workers who sit all day. Facilities concludes that mats cause the relief and will buy one for every desk. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Standing mats scuff more easily than standard chair mats do, which is a replacement-cost issue rather than a causal test.
options.b: Several workers already own a mat from a previous employer, which does not show that mats fail to reduce afternoon tightness.
options.c: Mat users also take more short walking breaks, a habit independently tied to less tightness.
options.d: The mats come in two colors, and most employees prefer gray, which does not explain which workers report less tightness.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-023.explanation: If walking breaks, not the mat, explain the tightness gap, buying mats for all desks will not deliver the claimed relief.

distractorExplanations.a: Scuffing is a maintenance issue, not a challenge to the causal claim.
distractorExplanations.b: Prior ownership does not show that mats fail to reduce tightness.
distractorExplanations.d: Color preference does not explain who reports less tightness.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-024.prompt: After Oakridge banned feeding deer in yards, vehicle collisions with deer rose the next winter. Opponents say the ban failed. Which finding, if true, most helps the town show the ban was not the cause of the rise?

options.a: Some residents continued to leave birdseed that deer also ate, which would show incomplete compliance rather than a clean test.
options.b: Wildlife cameras still recorded deer on Oakridge lawns after dusk, which speaks to leftover attractants, not to a shared winter cause.
options.c: The fine for feeding was smaller than the fine for overnight street parking, which does not identify what drove the collision spike that winter.
options.d: Neighboring towns without a feeding ban saw similar collision increases that winter.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-024.explanation: A parallel rise where feeding stayed legal points to a shared winter factor rather than Oakridge's ban as the cause of more collisions.

distractorExplanations.a: Continued feeding would, if anything, weaken the ban's implementation, not clear it of causing collisions.
distractorExplanations.b: Deer still on lawns speaks to compliance, not to whether the ban caused the crash spike.
distractorExplanations.c: Relative fine size does not identify the cause of the collision spike.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-025.prompt: Planners promoting walk-up apartments over shops argue that evening pedestrian counts rise where housing sits above cafes, cutting car errands. A comparison city that built housing without ground-floor retail saw evening walks rise only on streets that already had corner stores. Delivery vans then clustered on the storeless blocks. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Housing density lifts walking mainly where daily goods are already within a short walk.
options.b: Delivery vans appear only in cities that ban ground-floor cafes, even though vans clustered on the storeless housing blocks.
options.c: Evening pedestrian counts fall wherever apartments sit above cafes, even though mixed streets in the comparison gained pedestrians.
options.d: Corner stores reduce walking because shoppers drive between them, even though corner-store streets were the ones that gained walkers.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-025.explanation: The storeless housing blocks failed to raise evening walks and drew vans, while mixed streets gained pedestrians. That pattern ties walking gains to nearby daily goods, not to housing mass alone.

distractorExplanations.b: Vans clustered on storeless blocks; the text does not restrict vans to cafe-ban cities.
distractorExplanations.c: The argument's own examples include rising counts on mixed streets, not a universal fall.
distractorExplanations.d: Corner-store streets gained walkers; the text does not say stores induce driving between them.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-026.prompt: A clinic newsletter says a daily cup of kefir 'improves immunity' because regular drinkers reported fewer winter colds than non-drinkers. Which finding, if true, most weakens the causal claim?

options.a: Kefir brands vary in tartness from batch to batch, which cannot by itself create the reported winter-cold gap.
options.b: Kefir drinkers were also more likely to vaccinate and to stay home when symptomatic.
options.c: The newsletter was emailed on a Monday rather than a Friday, which is irrelevant to who reported fewer winter colds.
options.d: Some non-drinkers cited lactose discomfort as their reason for avoiding kefir, which explains avoidance, not why drinkers had fewer colds.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-026.explanation: Vaccination and staying home are independent cold-reducing behaviors that can create the reported gap without kefir causing immunity.

distractorExplanations.a: Tartness variation does not explain the cold-count difference.
distractorExplanations.c: Send-day of the newsletter is irrelevant to the drinkers' cold reports.
distractorExplanations.d: Lactose as a reason for abstaining does not show that drinkers' fewer colds are non-causal.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-027.prompt: Advocates say raising the city living wage will cut poverty because every covered worker's hourly rate will rise. Which consideration most weakens that prediction?

options.a: The living-wage ordinance was drafted by a bipartisan task force, which does not address hours, coverage, or annual earnings.
options.b: Some covered employers already pay above the proposed hourly floor, so those workplaces would not show the predicted poverty drop.
options.c: Hours may be cut, and uncovered contractors may replace some covered jobs.
options.d: Poverty statistics in the city are published only once each year, which is a measurement calendar, not a weakening of the earnings path.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-027.explanation: If hours fall or work shifts to uncovered contractors, a higher hourly floor need not raise annual earnings enough to cut poverty.

distractorExplanations.a: The drafters' party mix does not address the earnings mechanism.
distractorExplanations.b: Employers already above the floor are unaffected; that does not show covered workers will lose hours.
distractorExplanations.d: Publication frequency is a measurement detail, not a weakening of the predicted poverty drop.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-028.prompt: Health officials want a per-ounce levy on bottled sweet tea to cut sugar intake. Which finding, if true, most strengthens the case that the levy will reduce consumption?

options.a: Bottled sweet tea is cheaper to stock than sparkling water for many grocers, which does not show that buyers will cut ounces of sugar.
options.b: Tourists buy a large share of bottled tea at the airport, not in neighborhood stores, which could leak around a neighborhood levy rather than prove it.
options.c: The levy's revenue is earmarked for dental clinics rather than for schools, which affects clinics rather than the price-to-consumption link.
options.d: Shoppers in a similar city switched to unsweetened tea after an equivalent levy, with little cross-border shopping.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-028.explanation: A peer city's substitution toward unsweetened tea, without leakage across the border, is direct evidence that a like levy can cut sweet-tea intake.

distractorExplanations.a: Relative stocking cost does not show that buyers will cut sugar ounces.
distractorExplanations.b: Airport tourist purchases could leak around a neighborhood levy, which would weaken, not strengthen.
distractorExplanations.c: Revenue earmarks affect clinics, not the price-consumption link.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-029.prompt: When a non-native vine covered a floodplain forest, native understory herbs vanished and songbird nests failed more often, apparently because cats hunted more easily in the simplified layer. After a five-year pull program, herbs returned in patches, but vine fragments resprouted from root crowns left in wet soil. Bird nesting success recovered only in patches where herbs exceeded a cover threshold. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Partial vine removal can restore nesting only where understory cover also rebounds past a threshold.
options.b: Cats leave floodplain forests permanently once any vine is pulled after any vine stem is pulled from the floodplain forest.
options.c: Root-crown resprouts prove the vine cannot grow in wet soil, even though fragments resprouted from crowns left in wet soil.
options.d: Native herbs outcompete the vine even when no pulling occurs, even though the five-year pull program was what returned herb patches.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-029.explanation: Nesting recovered only above an herb-cover threshold after pulling, while remaining root crowns resprouted. That supports conditional, incomplete restoration, not a cat exodus or a vine that cannot handle wet soil.

distractorExplanations.b: Cats are discussed as hunters in simplified layers, not as permanently leaving after any pull.
distractorExplanations.c: Resprouts from wet-soil crowns show the vine can persist there, not that it cannot grow.
distractorExplanations.d: The pull program was needed; the text does not show herbs winning with no removal.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-030.prompt: Researchers claim that a nightly serving of walnuts lowers fasting triglycerides, citing volunteers who already ate walnuts and had lower readings than non-eaters. Which finding, if true, most weakens the claim?

options.a: Walnuts cost more per ounce than peanuts in the study's grocery sample, which cannot create the fasting-triglyceride gap by itself.
options.b: Walnut eaters also ran more miles per week, a habit independently tied to lower triglycerides.
options.c: The blood draws occurred on weekday mornings rather than weekends, so both walnut eaters and non-eaters were drawn the same way.
options.d: Some non-eaters said they disliked the texture of chopped walnuts, which explains avoidance, not the eaters' lower triglyceride readings.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-030.explanation: Extra mileage is a plausible alternate cause of the triglyceride gap, so walnut eating may only mark an already-active group.

distractorExplanations.a: Price does not create the biomarker difference.
distractorExplanations.c: Weekday draws, if applied to both groups, do not explain a between-group gap.
distractorExplanations.d: Texture dislike explains avoidance, not why eaters have lower triglycerides.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-031.prompt: Coders who wear noise-canceling headsets close more tickets per week than coders who work in open sound. The CTO concludes that headsets raise output and will require them. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Headset batteries need charging twice during a long shift, which is an inconvenience rather than a confounder of ticket counts.
options.b: The office already stocks extra headsets in a supply closet, which does not show that headsets caused the higher ticket counts.
options.c: Headset wearers were already the team's fastest debuggers before the devices arrived.
options.d: Some clients complain that headset users miss hallway questions, which is a communication cost rather than evidence against output gains.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-031.explanation: If wearers were already faster, the ticket gap is selection, not a headset effect, so a mandate is unjustified by these numbers.

distractorExplanations.a: Charging is an inconvenience, not a confounder of the output comparison.
distractorExplanations.b: Stock on hand does not address whether headsets caused higher ticket counts.
distractorExplanations.d: Missed hallway questions is a communication cost, not evidence against a causal output gain.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-032.prompt: A city will charge drivers a daily cordon fee to enter downtown, expecting congestion to fall. Which finding, if true, most weakens that expectation?

options.a: Downtown parking meters already use a mobile-pay app, which does not show that cordon trips will disappear at peak.
options.b: Bus routes into downtown run every twelve minutes at peak, which would, if anything, give drivers a substitute for paying the fee.
options.c: The fee is lower than the average lunch cost at downtown cafes, which does not show that inelastic peak trips will stop driving in.
options.d: Many peak trips are deliveries and care workers who cannot shift time or mode.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-032.explanation: If a large share of peak trips cannot switch time or mode, the fee will collect money without much traffic reduction.

distractorExplanations.a: Meter apps are orthogonal to whether trips disappear from the cordon.
distractorExplanations.b: Frequent buses would, if anything, help the fee work by offering a substitute.
distractorExplanations.c: Comparison to lunch prices does not show that inelastic trips will keep driving.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-033.prompt: Eastbridge Transit says new express buses on Route 12 will cut average door-to-door time for current Route 12 riders. Which assumption is required?

options.a: Time lost walking to fewer express stops will not wipe out the in-vehicle time saved.
options.b: Route 12 buses will be painted a new color to distinguish expresses, which does not determine door-to-door time for current riders.
options.c: Fares on the express will be identical to local fares on day one, which is a pricing choice rather than a required time premise.
options.d: Neighboring Route 14 already runs an express in the opposite direction, which is unused in the Route 12 door-to-door time argument.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-033.explanation: Door-to-door time falls only if station-access penalties do not consume the faster ride. That net-time assumption is required.

distractorExplanations.b: Paint color does not determine door-to-door time.
distractorExplanations.c: Fare equality is a pricing choice, not required for the time claim.
distractorExplanations.d: A different route's express is unused in the Route 12 time argument.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-034.prompt: Dune Mutual raised premiums 12 percent on cottages within two miles of the tide line, citing higher storm-surge claims. Which finding, if true, most weakens the justification?

options.a: Some cottages are used only in summer, not in hurricane months, so some policies cover months with little storm-surge exposure.
options.b: Claims in the band rose because a few outlier mansions flooded, while typical cottages' loss rates were flat.
options.c: Reinsurers offered Dune Mutual a slightly lower treaty rate this year, which would ease, not tighten, pressure to raise cottage premiums.
options.d: Tide-line maps used by the assessor were last redrawn a decade ago, which is a mapping caveat rather than a claim about claims composition.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-034.explanation: If the average cottage's losses were flat and a few mansions drove the mean, a blanket 12 percent on all cottages is not justified by typical risk.

distractorExplanations.a: Seasonal use might cut exposure but does not show the cited claims spike is misleading.
distractorExplanations.c: A cheaper treaty would, if anything, ease pressure to raise premiums.
distractorExplanations.d: Stale maps could be a separate issue; they do not show the claims composition is skewed.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-035.prompt: Many drivers assume a higher rural speed limit must raise fatalities. After Lark State lifted the limit on two-lane roads, fatalities per mile fell slightly. Which finding, if true, most helps reconcile the result with the common assumption?

options.a: Lark State's gasoline tax rose in the same budget year, which does not obviously offset speed risk on two-lane rural roads.
options.b: Tourist brochures still listed the old limit for six months, which would delay, not reverse, any fatality effect of the new limit.
options.c: The state also added rumble strips and closed several high-crash passing zones when the limit changed.
options.d: Motorcycle registrations in Lark State were little changed that year, which removes one confound but does not explain a fatality drop.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-035.explanation: Engineering fixes introduced with the limit can cut deaths even if speed itself is riskier, reconciling a fatality drop with the usual speed-death link.

distractorExplanations.a: A gas-tax change does not obviously offset speed risk on two-lane roads.
distractorExplanations.b: Stale brochures would delay, not reverse, a fatality effect of the new limit.
distractorExplanations.d: Stable motorcycle counts remove one confound but do not explain a fatality drop under a higher limit.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-037.prompt: A column claims winter vitamin D capsules prevent colds because capsule users reported fewer sick days than non-users. Which finding, if true, most weakens the claim?

options.a: Capsules were sold in both 1,000- and 2,000-unit strengths, which does not by itself create a user versus non-user sick-day gap.
options.b: Some non-users said they already spent weekends outdoors, which would, if anything, give non-users more sunlight-related vitamin D.
options.c: The column appeared in a fitness magazine rather than a medical journal, which is not evidence about whether capsules prevent winter colds.
options.d: Capsule users were also more likely to work from home, reducing exposure to office viruses.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-037.explanation: Work-from-home cuts exposure and can produce fewer sick days without vitamin D doing the work, undercutting the causal column.

distractorExplanations.a: Dose strength variation does not by itself create a user/non-user gap.
distractorExplanations.b: Outdoor weekends among non-users would, if anything, give non-users more vitamin D, which would not explain users' fewer sick days.
distractorExplanations.c: Venue of publication is not evidence about the causal mechanism.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-038.prompt: After Pell County replaced paper parking permits with a phone app, fine revenue fell 30 percent in year one. The treasurer says residents became more law-abiding. Which finding, if true, most weakens that explanation?

options.a: Enforcement officers spent months learning the app and issued far fewer tickets than before.
options.b: The app displayed a digital clock on the home screen, which does not explain a 30 percent drop in parking-fine revenue.
options.c: Paper permits had been printed on recycled stock, which is irrelevant to whether residents became more law-abiding.
options.d: Nearby counties still used paper hangtags on their meters, which cannot explain why Pell County's fine revenue fell.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-038.explanation: If ticketing effort collapsed during the learning period, revenue can fall without any rise in compliance.

distractorExplanations.b: A clock display does not explain a 30 percent revenue drop.
distractorExplanations.c: Recycled paper is irrelevant to compliance or revenue.
distractorExplanations.d: Neighbors' hangtags do not explain Pell's revenue change.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-039.prompt: A marine lab argues that warmer water, not farm runoff, caused a kelp die-off, because satellite temperatures rose in the same months kelp canopy shrank. Which finding, if true, most weakens that argument?

options.a: Kelp canopies also shrank in a colder bay farther north, which lacks the same-heat, low-runoff contrast the cove provides.
options.b: Runoff spikes coincided with the heat, and a protected cove with the same heat but no runoff kept its kelp.
options.c: Tourist kayak rentals near the die-off fell that summer, which is an economic side effect rather than a cause of kelp loss.
options.d: The satellite series has a two-kilometer resolution along the coast, which is a measurement caveat rather than a direct alternative cause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-039.explanation: A same-heat, low-runoff cove that kept kelp, plus simultaneous runoff, offers a comparison that points to pollution rather than heat alone.

distractorExplanations.a: A colder bay's loss would, if anything, also challenge a heat-only story, but without a runoff contrast it is weaker than the cove comparison.
distractorExplanations.c: Kayak rentals are an economic side effect, not a cause of the die-off.
distractorExplanations.d: Coarser resolution is a measurement caveat, not a direct alternative cause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-040.prompt: Since a dockless e-scooter program launched, emergency-room visits for street injuries rose 15 percent. A council member blames the scooters. Which finding, if true, most weakens that blame?

options.a: Scooter riders must watch a safety video before unlocking a vehicle, which would, if anything, cut scooter injuries rather than raise ER visits.
options.b: The city painted additional bicycle lanes in the same year, which would more likely protect cyclists than explain more ER visits.
options.c: A tourism festival and a new downtown stadium opened that year, raising pedestrian and car traffic independently.
options.d: Scooter batteries are swapped at night by contractors on cargo bikes, which does not account for a citywide rise in street-injury visits.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-040.explanation: Extra festival and stadium traffic can lift injury visits without scooters being the driver of the 15 percent rise.

distractorExplanations.a: A safety video would, if anything, cut scooter injuries, not explain the rise.
distractorExplanations.b: New bike lanes would more likely protect cyclists than explain more ER visits.
distractorExplanations.d: Nighttime battery swaps do not account for a citywide injury-visit increase.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-041.prompt: A cafe chain finds that shops with counter tablets sell 10 percent more pastry add-ons per customer than shops with only cashiers. Managers conclude that tablets cause the extra sales. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Tablets sometimes freeze during the breakfast rush, which would hinder, not create, extra pastry add-on sales per customer.
options.b: Cashiers receive the same pastry commission as tablet-assisted shops, which removes one incentive difference but leaves the location confound.
options.c: Some customers pay with cash even at tablet counters, which does not show that tablets fail to prompt extra pastry add-ons.
options.d: The tablet shops were already the busiest locations before the devices were installed.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-041.explanation: If tablet shops were already high-volume, the add-on gap can be location, not the interface, so the causal conclusion is unsupported.

distractorExplanations.a: Freezing would hinder, not create, extra add-on sales.
distractorExplanations.b: Equal commission removes one incentive difference but leaves the location confound untouched.
distractorExplanations.c: Cash at a tablet counter does not show that tablets fail to prompt extra pastry add-ons.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-042.prompt: E-cargo bike sales in Portmead doubled last year, yet the share of workers who commute by bicycle was unchanged. Which finding, if true, best explains the pair of facts?

options.a: Most new e-cargo bikes were bought by bakeries and grocers for local deliveries, not by commuters.
options.b: Portmead added two miles of painted bike lanes on a waterfront path, which would more likely raise commuter share than hold it flat.
options.c: E-cargo bikes weigh more than ordinary road bikes when unloaded, which is a design fact rather than an explanation of who bought them.
options.d: A nearby city reported a small rise in weekend recreational cycling, which does not account for Portmead's sales-versus-commute split.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-042.explanation: If commercial deliveries absorbed the sales boom, commuter mode share can sit still while unit sales double.

distractorExplanations.b: New lanes would more likely raise commuter share, not hold it flat.
distractorExplanations.c: Weight is a design fact, not an explanation of who bought the extra bikes.
distractorExplanations.d: Another city's recreation trend does not account for Portmead's sales-versus-commute split.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-043.prompt: After Millford's pool offered free child lessons, reported child drownings in open water rose the next summer. Critics say the lessons failed. Which finding, if true, most helps the city reply?

options.a: The pool's hours expanded into weekday evenings, which would increase supervised pool time rather than quarry drownings.
options.b: A heat wave drew many more children to unsupervised quarries, raising exposure independent of lessons.
options.c: Lesson badges were printed on waterproof paper, which is irrelevant to the open-water drowning trend the next summer.
options.d: Adult lap swim remained ticketed at the same price, which does not affect how many children entered unsupervised water.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-043.explanation: A heat-driven jump in quarry swimming can lift drownings even if lessons helped those who took them, so the rise does not show the program failed.

distractorExplanations.a: Longer pool hours would tend to increase supervised swim time, not explain more open-water deaths.
distractorExplanations.c: Badge paper is irrelevant to the drowning trend.
distractorExplanations.d: Adult lap prices do not affect child open-water exposure.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-044.prompt: Agronomists say a new three-crop rotation, not a wet spring, explains higher wheat yields in Hollow County. Which finding, if true, most strengthens that claim?

options.a: Wheat futures prices rose in the same marketing year, which does not identify what raised physical wheat yields in Hollow.
options.b: Hollow County's extension office mailed a rotation pamphlet in February, which shows outreach rather than that rotation beat the wet spring.
options.c: Neighboring Ridge County had the same wet spring but kept two-crop rotation and saw no yield jump.
options.d: Some Hollow farms still plant a winter cover that is not part of the new rotation, which would blur, not sharpen, the county-wide rotation attribution.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-044.explanation: A same-weather neighbor without the rotation and without the yield jump isolates rotation as the differing factor.

distractorExplanations.a: Futures prices do not identify what raised physical yields.
distractorExplanations.b: Mailing a pamphlet shows outreach, not that rotation rather than rain did the work.
distractorExplanations.d: Farms skipping the new rotation would, if anything, blur the county-wide attribution.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-045.prompt: Diggers found charred millet grains in a hearth dated 8,500 years ago and concluded the occupants farmed millet. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: The hearth stones show repeated heating and cooling cracks, which confirms a cooking fire rather than sown millet agriculture.
options.b: Millet straw can be used as animal bedding in later periods, which concerns later periods rather than this 8,500-year-old hearth.
options.c: A nearby stream could have flooded the terrace in spring, which does not identify the grains as morphologically wild versus sown.
options.d: The grains match a wild millet that sheds easily and was likely gathered, not sown.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-045.explanation: If the grains are morphologically wild and shatter-prone, gathering explains their presence without cultivation.

distractorExplanations.a: Heat cracks confirm a hearth, not farming.
distractorExplanations.b: Later bedding use does not speak to this 8,500-year-old deposit.
distractorExplanations.c: A possible flood is speculative and does not identify the grains as wild versus sown.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-046.prompt: To lift sales of its house-brand crackers, a grocer will move them to eye-level shelves now used by national brands. Which assumption is required?

options.a: Shoppers who now grab national crackers at eye level will sometimes take the house brand once it occupies that space.
options.b: The house-brand box will be redesigned in a brighter color before the move, which is a separate marketing choice, not required by shelf height.
options.c: National brands will not lower their wholesale prices in response, which would matter for margins, not for the placement mechanism.
options.d: The grocer's warehouse already holds extra cases of house-brand crackers, which is an operations detail, not a logical requirement of the plan.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-046.explanation: The plan works only if eye-level placement actually switches some buyers. Without that substitution, moving boxes will not lift house-brand sales.

distractorExplanations.b: A color redesign is a separate marketing choice, not required by the shelf-height mechanism.
distractorExplanations.c: National price responses would matter for margins, not for the stated placement mechanism.
distractorExplanations.d: Warehouse stock is an operations detail, not a logical requirement of the sales argument.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-047.prompt: After Brookbend installed brighter lamps on Maple Avenue, reported night crashes on that street fell. The engineer credits the lamps. Which finding, if true, most weakens that credit?

options.a: Lamp posts were painted a darker green than the previous fixtures, which does not explain why reported night crashes on Maple fell.
options.b: The city also retimed the Maple Avenue signals and added a mid-block crossing the same month.
options.c: Nearby Elm Street still uses the older, dimmer fixtures, which is a contrast street rather than a confound on Maple Avenue.
options.d: Some residents said the new lamps felt harsh on bedroom windows, which is a nuisance complaint rather than an alternative crash cause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-047.explanation: Signal timing and a new crossing are independent safety changes that can cut crashes without the lamps being responsible.

distractorExplanations.a: Post color does not explain a crash decline.
distractorExplanations.c: Elm Street's dimmer lamps are a contrast, not a confound on Maple.
distractorExplanations.d: Bedroom glare is a nuisance complaint, not an alternative crash-reduction cause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-048.prompt: A studio moved to a four-day on-site week. Over the next half year, client-reported defects in its apps fell. Leadership credits extra rest. Which finding, if true, most weakens that explanation?

options.a: Some staff still answered weekend chat messages, which would cut rest and so would not explain fewer defects via rest.
options.b: The studio's kitchen stocked better coffee after the change, which is a weak alternative compared with shipping a new test suite.
options.c: In the same week as the calendar change, the studio shipped a long-delayed automated test suite.
options.d: A rival studio kept a five-day on-site week, which does not explain this studio's drop in client-reported defects.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-048.explanation: A new test suite can catch defects before clients see them, so the drop need not come from rest.

distractorExplanations.a: Weekend chat would cut rest, which would not explain fewer defects via the rest theory.
distractorExplanations.b: Coffee quality is a weak, unrelated alternative compared with a testing-system launch.
distractorExplanations.d: A rival's calendar does not explain this studio's defect drop.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-049.prompt: Every scooter sold by Nox Motion includes a two-year battery warranty. Some Nox scooters are sold to rental fleets. Nox's city scooters are all rental-fleet sales. Which conclusion must be true?

options.a: No privately owned Nox scooter has a battery warranty, even though the premises give every Nox scooter the battery warranty.
options.b: Every rental-fleet scooter in the city is made by Nox Motion, even though other brands may also sell scooters to the city fleets.
options.c: Nox's city scooters lack battery warranties because fleets self-insure, even though the premises assign warranties to every Nox scooter sold.
options.d: Every Nox city scooter comes with the two-year battery warranty.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-049.explanation: City scooters are Nox rental-fleet sales, and every Nox scooter—including fleet units—has the warranty, so every city scooter has it.

distractorExplanations.a: Private sales are not shown to lack warranties; all Nox scooters have them.
distractorExplanations.b: Other brands may also sell to city fleets; the premises never close that door.
distractorExplanations.c: Self-insurance is invented; the premises assign warranties to every Nox scooter.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-050.prompt: A district says students in its new evening algebra clinic raised grades more than classmates who skipped it, so the clinic works. Which finding, if true, most weakens that inference?

options.a: Clinic joiners were already higher-scoring and had tutors, and they attended more class days than skippers.
options.b: The clinic used the same textbook as the daytime course, which would, if anything, make clinic joiners and skippers more comparable.
options.c: Buses home from the clinic ran on time on most evenings, which is a logistics plus rather than a reason skippers earned weaker grades.
options.d: Some skippers played a sport that ended after 6 p.m, which is a narrower alternative than prior scores, tutors, and attendance.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-050.explanation: Pre-existing achievement, tutors, and attendance can produce the grade gap without the clinic causing it.

distractorExplanations.b: A shared textbook would, if anything, make the groups more comparable.
distractorExplanations.c: On-time buses are a logistics plus, not a confounder that explains skippers' weaker grades.
distractorExplanations.d: Sports among skippers might matter but is narrower than the bundle of prior score, tutors, and attendance.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-051.prompt: To draw more visitors under 30, a maritime museum will add touchscreen ship simulators. Which finding, if true, most weakens the plan's reasoning?

options.a: The simulators require a staff member nearby during busy hours, which objects to operations, not to whether screens attract visitors under 30.
options.b: Younger visitors already come for the outdoor dry-dock; indoor screens do not change their attendance.
options.c: A history museum in another city uses audio guides rather than screens, which does not show that simulators will fail to draw this museum's audience.
options.d: The simulators can display both sail and steam vessel types, which does not weaken the claim that screens will change under-30 attendance.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-051.explanation: If the under-30 audience is already coming for the dry-dock and ignores indoor screens, the simulators will not deliver the targeted attendance gain.

distractorExplanations.a: Staffing cost objects to operations, not to whether screens attract younger visitors.
distractorExplanations.c: Another museum's audio guides do not show screens will fail here.
distractorExplanations.d: Sail versus steam display range does not weaken the attendance mechanism.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-053.prompt: Researchers note that towns with more public libraries per resident have higher adult literacy, and they conclude that building libraries raises literacy. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Some libraries host evening knitting groups in their meeting rooms, which is an extra use of rooms rather than an alternative literacy cause.
options.b: Library construction costs vary with local land prices, which affects construction cost rather than the causal reading of the correlation.
options.c: Wealth and schooling independently produce both more libraries and higher literacy, reversing the proposed cause.
options.d: A few towns closed a branch on Sundays last year, which is a minor schedule change rather than a confounder of the town pattern.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-053.explanation: If wealth and schooling jointly generate libraries and literacy, the correlation is confounded and building libraries need not raise literacy.

distractorExplanations.a: Knitting groups are an extra use of space, not an alternative cause of the literacy correlation.
distractorExplanations.b: Land prices affect cost, not the causal reading of the correlation.
distractorExplanations.d: Sunday closures are a minor schedule change, not a confounder of the town-level pattern.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-054.prompt: In Basin Q, every orchard that grows pears also grows apples. Some apple orchards in Basin Q use frost fans. No pear orchard uses drip lines. Which conclusion must be true?

options.a: Every apple orchard in Basin Q grows pears as well, since pears imply apples in Basin Q, not the reverse pairing.
options.b: Some pear orchards in Basin Q use frost fans, since fans on some apple orchards need not include any pear orchard.
options.c: No apple orchard in Basin Q uses frost fans, since the premises already say some apple orchards in Basin Q use fans.
options.d: No pear orchard in Basin Q uses drip lines, including those that also grow apples.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-054.explanation: The last premise already states that no pear orchard uses drip lines. Pear-and-apple orchards are still pear orchards, so they too lack drip lines. The other options reverse or overreach the some/every statements.

distractorExplanations.a: Pears imply apples, not the reverse; apple-only orchards may exist.
distractorExplanations.b: Fans on some apple orchards need not include any pear orchard.
distractorExplanations.c: The premises say some apple orchards use fans, so this universal denial is false.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-056.prompt: Some managers say remote work wrecks culture because people rarely share a kitchen. A critic replies that culture is mainly shared standards for decisions, which can be taught in writing. Which option most accurately describes the critic's technique?

options.a: The critic redefines culture so that physical proximity is no longer essential to it.
options.b: The critic presents a survey of remote workers' favorite snacks, which never appears in the critic's reply about shared decision standards.
options.c: The critic argues that kitchens are more expensive to maintain than office software, which is a budget comparison the critic does not actually offer.
options.d: The critic claims remote work raises measured output per hour, which is a productivity claim the critic does not actually make.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-056.explanation: Managers treat kitchen contact as culture; the critic substitutes decision standards that do not require a kitchen, which is a definitional shift.

distractorExplanations.b: No snack survey appears in the critic's reply.
distractorExplanations.c: Cost of kitchens versus software is not the critic's move.
distractorExplanations.d: Output per hour is a productivity claim the critic does not make.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-057.prompt: HR notes that staff who attend optional posture workshops take fewer sick days and concludes the workshops cut illness. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Workshops are held in a room with large windows, which does not explain the sick-day gap between attendees and others.
options.b: Attendees were already more health-conscious and used fewer sick days before the series began.
options.c: The instructor also teaches a weekend climbing class off-site, which is unused in HR's claim that workshops cut illness.
options.d: HR printed attendance badges on recycled card stock, which is irrelevant to whether workshops reduced recorded sick days.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-057.explanation: A pre-existing health gap means workshops may only attract people who were going to be well anyway.

distractorExplanations.a: Windows do not explain the sick-day comparison.
distractorExplanations.c: An off-site climbing class is unused in the HR causal claim.
distractorExplanations.d: Badge paper is irrelevant to illness rates.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-058.prompt: An online poll on a trail-running forum found that 82 percent of respondents support a new riverside path. Advocates cite the poll as proof of citywide support. Which criticism is most to the point?

options.a: The poll used a 1-to-5 scale on one of its other questions, which does not create the sampling problem in the citywide citation.
options.b: Some respondents typed extra comments in a free-text box, which does not make a trail-running forum a representative city sample.
options.c: Forum members are already path enthusiasts, so the sample overrepresents supporters relative to the city.
options.d: The path would need lighting if it stayed open after dusk, which is a design issue rather than a critique of the poll's sample.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-058.explanation: A self-selected enthusiast forum is not a city sample; citing 82 percent as citywide support is a biased-sample error.

distractorExplanations.a: A scale on another item does not create the sampling problem.
distractorExplanations.b: Free-text comments do not make the sample representative.
distractorExplanations.d: Lighting is a design issue, not a critique of the poll's representativeness.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-059.prompt: A mayor says 75 percent of office complaints last year were about overflowing bins, so bins are residents' biggest problem. Which option most accurately describes a flaw?

options.a: It assumes bins overflow only in summer heat, which is not the leap from complaint share to residents' biggest problem.
options.b: It fails to count how many bins the city owns, which is unused in the inference from complaint volume to importance.
options.c: It treats overflowing bins as more expensive to fix than potholes, which is not the mayor's measure; the argument uses complaint counts.
options.d: It equates complaint volume with importance, ignoring that bin issues are easy to report and other harms go unfiled.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-059.explanation: Complaint share can reflect ease of reporting, not ranking of harms. The mayor treats the 75 percent as a welfare ranking without that link.

distractorExplanations.a: Seasonality of overflow is not the mayor's stated leap.
distractorExplanations.b: Inventory of bins is unused in the importance inference.
distractorExplanations.c: Repair cost is not the argument's measure; complaint counts are.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-060.prompt: A reviewer says a poet's new collection sold fewer copies than her debut, so her craft has declined. Which criticism is most to the point?

options.a: Sales can fall because the debut's novelty faded or the market shrank, which need not mean weaker poems.
options.b: The reviewer quotes only one stanza from the new collection, which is a review-style complaint rather than the sales-to-quality flaw.
options.c: Poetry collections rarely appear on bestseller lists, which does not specifically explain this author's drop in copies sold.
options.d: The debut was published in hardcover and the new book in paperback, which might affect price, but the core flaw is treating sales as craft.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-060.explanation: The argument infers quality from units sold. Alternative commercial explanations sever that inference without denying a sales drop.

distractorExplanations.b: Quoting one stanza is a review-style complaint, not the core sales-to-quality flaw.
distractorExplanations.c: Bestseller rarity does not specifically explain this author's drop.
distractorExplanations.d: Format change might affect price, but the decisive flaw is using sales as a craft meter.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-061.prompt: When a regional carrier cut fares 18 percent, total ticket revenue rose even though it added no flights. Which finding, if true, most helps explain the revenue rise?

options.a: The carrier's coffee service was unchanged after the cut, which does not explain why total ticket revenue rose after the fare cut.
options.b: The fare cut filled many previously empty seats, and extra passengers more than offset the lower price.
options.c: Rival carriers painted their tails in new colors that year, which is unrelated to this carrier's price-times-quantity revenue identity.
options.d: The carrier's pilots had recently signed a multiyear contract, which affects costs rather than the fare-cut arithmetic for ticket revenue.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-061.explanation: Revenue is price times quantity. Filling empty seats can raise the product even when price falls, which fits no added flights.

distractorExplanations.a: Coffee service does not explain a revenue jump after a fare cut.
distractorExplanations.c: Rivals' paint schemes are unrelated to this carrier's revenue identity.
distractorExplanations.d: A pilot contract affects costs, not the fare-to-revenue arithmetic.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-062.prompt: All of this summer's interns at Helix Bio are biochemistry majors. Some of the interns received travel grants. No chemistry-department faculty member received a travel grant. Which conclusion must be true?

options.a: Every biochemistry major at Helix Bio is a summer intern, since the premises run from interns to majors, not the reverse.
options.b: Some chemistry-department faculty members are biochemistry majors, since the premises never mention faculty members' undergraduate majors.
options.c: None of the travel-grant interns is a chemistry-department faculty member.
options.d: All travel grants at Helix Bio went to biochemistry majors, since people outside the intern pool might still have received grants.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-062.explanation: Grant-holding interns are biochemistry majors and interns; faculty got no grants. Therefore no grant intern is a chemistry faculty member. The other choices reverse or expand the premises.

distractorExplanations.a: Interns are biochemistry majors, not the reverse.
distractorExplanations.b: Nothing in the premises shows chemistry faculty overlapping with biochemistry majors.
distractorExplanations.d: Grants to people outside the intern pool are not ruled out.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-063.prompt: Hospital North posts a higher death rate among surgical patients than Hospital South, yet surgeons still call North the stronger trauma center. Which finding, if true, most helps reconcile the two claims?

options.a: Hospital North's cafeteria scores higher on patient surveys, which does not explain a higher raw death rate among surgical patients.
options.b: Hospital South performs more outpatient wart removals than North, which might dilute South's rate without showing that North is more skilled.
options.c: Parking is cheaper in Hospital South's garage than in North's, which is irrelevant to reconciling reputation with crude surgical deaths.
options.d: North accepts a far higher share of unstable transfers, so its mix is sicker even if its surgical skill is greater.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-063.explanation: A sicker incoming mix can raise raw death rates at a more capable trauma center, reconciling reputation with the crude statistic.

distractorExplanations.a: Cafeteria scores do not explain surgical death rates.
distractorExplanations.b: Wart removals at South would lower South's death rate by diluting the denominator, which could widen North's gap but does not show North is stronger.
distractorExplanations.c: Parking prices are irrelevant to surgical outcomes.
