gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-064.prompt: A village replaced all-night street lamps with motion-triggered LEDs, and the lighting electricity bill fell 40 percent. Officials credit the sensors. Which finding, if true, most weakens that credit?

options.a: The village also cut the nightly hours of two floodlit sports fields in the same billing period.
options.b: LED bulbs last longer than the sodium lamps they replaced, which affects replacement cost more than this period's electricity bill.
options.c: A neighboring village still uses all-night sodium lamps, which does not explain why this village's lighting bill fell 40 percent.
options.d: Some residents said the new lights flicker when a cat walks by, which is a comfort complaint rather than an alternative energy-saving cause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-064.explanation: Losing sports-field flood hours can crash the lighting bill without the street sensors doing the work.

distractorExplanations.b: Longer bulb life affects replacement cost, not this period's electricity bill as directly as field hours.
distractorExplanations.c: A neighbor's old lamps do not explain this village's bill drop.
distractorExplanations.d: Flicker complaints are comfort issues, not an alternative energy-saving cause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065.prompt: To cut cashier turnover, Northgate Mart will raise starting pay 8 percent. Exit interviews say most leavers complained about unpredictable schedules, not pay. Which finding, if true, most weakens the raise-as-solution plan?

options.a: A rival grocer already pays a few cents more per hour, which is a market comparison rather than evidence that schedules drive exits.
options.b: Leavers who cited schedules would have stayed for stable hours even without an 8 percent raise.
options.c: Northgate's training videos are due for an update next quarter, which is unrelated to the exit interviews that named unpredictable hours.
options.d: Some cashiers use the employee discount on produce, which does not address whether an 8 percent raise is the turnover lever.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065.explanation: If the binding complaint is hours, and people would stay for stable rosters without more pay, the raise will not hit the stated turnover cause.

distractorExplanations.a: A rival's wage is a market fact, not evidence that schedules—not pay—drive exits.
distractorExplanations.c: Training videos are unrelated to the exit-interview diagnosis.
distractorExplanations.d: Produce discounts do not address whether pay is the lever for turnover.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066.prompt: Supporters of a checkout-bag fee in Redhill say it will cut plastic litter in creeks. Which finding, if true, most weakens that prediction?

options.a: The fee is collected by cashiers rather than by an automated kiosk, which does not determine whether creek plastic litter will actually fall.
options.b: Redhill already recycles cardboard at two depots, which does not speak to plastic checkout-bag litter in Redhill's creeks in the period at issue.
options.c: Shoppers will switch to thicker 'reuse' bags that are still plastic and are discarded after a few trips, leaving creek plastic little changed.
options.d: A neighboring town prints the fee amount on receipts, which is irrelevant to whether Redhill shoppers will abandon thin bags.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066.explanation: If the substitute is still short-lived plastic, creek litter need not fall, which undercuts the supporters' environmental prediction.

distractorExplanations.a: Who collects the fee does not determine litter outcomes.
distractorExplanations.b: Cardboard depots do not speak to plastic bag litter in creeks.
distractorExplanations.d: Receipt printing in another town is irrelevant to Redhill's litter path.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067.prompt: A textbook house plans to lift profit by selling only digital editions, since file distribution is cheaper than printing. Which assumption is required?

options.a: Students prefer highlighting on glass to marking paper margins, which is unused in the cost-saving story about dropping print runs.
options.b: Campus bookstores will display the publisher's titles in their windows, which is a marketing extra rather than a necessary profit premise.
options.c: The publisher will cut the list price of each title by the printing savings, which would pass savings to buyers and so would not secure extra profit.
options.d: Any lost sales from students who refuse screens will not exceed the cost savings on copies that still sell.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067.explanation: Profit rises only if print-cost savings outrun revenue lost from print-only buyers. That net-profit assumption is required.

distractorExplanations.a: Highlighting preference is not required for the cost-saving profit story.
distractorExplanations.b: Bookstore window display is a marketing extra, not a necessary premise.
distractorExplanations.c: Passing savings into list price would reduce, not secure, the profit claim.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065-du.prompt: Over four years, average exam scores at Cedar Ridge High rose. The principal credits a new advisory period. Which finding, if true, most weakens that credit?

options.a: The district also replaced the exam with an easier form and raised course grades through a new curve in the same years.
options.b: Advisory groups meet in homeroom rather than in the gym, which does not explain a four-year rise in average exam scores.
options.c: Some teachers assign weekend reading during advisory weeks, which would add work rather than inflate reported exam scores.
options.d: A nearby high school kept its old schedule and saw stable sports wins, which is unrelated to Cedar Ridge's reported exam-score series.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065-du.explanation: An easier exam and a gentler curve can lift reported scores without advisory periods causing more learning.

distractorExplanations.b: Meeting room choice does not explain a four-year score rise.
distractorExplanations.c: Weekend reading would, if anything, add work, not an alternative inflation of scores.
distractorExplanations.d: A neighbor's sports record is unrelated to Cedar Ridge scores.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066-du.prompt: Registered voters in Hillford rose 9 percent between two elections, yet votes cast fell. Which finding, if true, most helps explain the pair?

options.a: Hillford printed extra ballots in case of a recount, which is unused inventory rather than an explanation of votes cast.
options.b: The registration drive signed up many people who never intended to turn out, while loyal voters moved away.
options.c: Polling places stayed open until 8 p.m. both years, which does not split a larger roll from a smaller number of ballots.
options.d: A local radio host discussed the election on a weekday morning, which does not specifically add registrants while subtracting voters.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066-du.explanation: Adding non-voting registrants while losing actual voters can raise the roll and cut ballots cast at the same time.

distractorExplanations.a: Extra printed ballots are unused inventory, not an explanation of turnout.
distractorExplanations.c: Unchanged poll hours do not split registration from votes.
distractorExplanations.d: A radio segment does not specifically produce more registrants and fewer votes.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067-du.prompt: An economist says a weaker currency should lift a country's trade balance because exports cheapen for foreigners. After the currency fell, the trade balance worsened. Which finding, if true, most helps explain the surprise?

options.a: Tourist brochures were not reprinted for six weeks, which is too minor to reverse a national trade-balance prediction.
options.b: The central bank published the exchange rate on its website, which is a transparency step rather than a cost channel for exporters.
options.c: Domestic firms rely on imported parts billed in foreign currency, so export costs rose with the depreciation, which does not explain import-cost pass-through on the country's exports.
options.d: A trading partner's soccer team won a regional tournament that month.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067-du.explanation: If exporters' imported inputs rise in local cost as the currency falls, export prices need not become more competitive, so the trade balance can worsen.

distractorExplanations.a: Brochure lag is too minor to reverse a national trade-balance prediction.
distractorExplanations.b: Publishing the rate is transparency, not a cost channel.
distractorExplanations.c: A soccer result does not explain import-cost pass-through on exports.
